name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
title: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
answer: Valuing illiquid tokens covers digital assets that cannot be sold quickly at a quoted market price without moving the price or breaching a lockup. It includes restricted tokens, vesting schedules, private sale positions, low float tokens, and positions in thin decentralized exchange pools. The work sits in digital asset accounting because carrying values, impairment tests, fund net asset values, and tax reports all need a defensible price. It is distinct from liquid token pricing, where an exchange quote or a volume weighted average price can often serve as the starting point.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Valuing illiquid tokens covers digital assets that cannot be sold quickly at a quoted market price without moving the price or breaching a lockup. It includes restricted tokens, vesting schedules, private sale positions, low float tokens, and positions in thin decentralized exchange pools. The work sits in digital asset accounting because carrying values, impairment tests, fund net asset values, and tax reports all need a defensible price. It is distinct from liquid token pricing, where an exchange quote or a volume weighted average price can often serve as the starting point.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on data rather than a single price feed. Practitioners pull on chain records such as vesting contracts, wallet labels, transfer restrictions, and pool reserves, then combine them with order book depth, trade history, and comparable private transactions. Spreadsheets, valuation models, and data warehouses are common, and some teams use market data providers or blockchain analytics platforms to normalize the inputs. The infrastructure must preserve source timestamps and raw data because a later audit or dispute will ask where each number came from.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with a unit definition and a restriction analysis, because a locked token and a freely tradable token are not the same asset. Teams then choose an approach, often a market approach using observed prices with liquidity and marketability adjustments, an income approach using projected cash flows or staking rewards, or a cost approach for very early positions. Adjustments may include discounts for lack of marketability, blockage, or control, and the result is tested with sensitivity ranges. Documentation records the inputs, the model, the rationale, and the date of valuation.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance covers rights, risk, and provenance. The valuation file needs a clear chain of custody for prices, wallet data, legal agreements, and any third party inputs, plus sign off from accounting, compliance, and sometimes an independent reviewer. Risks include stale data, wash trading, oracle manipulation, unregistered securities questions, and transfer restrictions that change without notice. Provenance matters because a price without a source, a timestamp, and a method is not audit evidence. The site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages, which reflects how much of this work depends on policy and disclosure rather than arithmetic alone.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The horizon points toward more continuous and more automated valuation. Tokenization of private assets, broader use of lockups and vesting, and better on chain disclosure are likely to increase the number of illiquid positions that need a price. AI assisted comparables, anomaly detection, and document extraction may reduce manual effort, but they do not remove the need for judgment and review. Regulators and standard setters are likely to keep pressing for consistent fair value and disclosure, so the practice will keep moving closer to traditional private asset valuation.
